name: Canagliflozin
route_note: oral tablet 100 or 300 mg once daily before the first meal
owner: Janssen (Johnson & Johnson); Mitsubishi Tanabe in Japan
tagline: First SGLT2 inhibitor in the US, and the first to show kidney benefit (CREDENCE)
summary: Canagliflozin was the first SGLT2 inhibitor approved in the United States (2013). It lowers glucose by increasing urinary glucose excretion; the CANVAS programme showed cardiovascular benefit but raised an amputation signal, and CREDENCE showed it slows diabetic kidney disease.
mechanism: The sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2, gene SLC5A2) in the early proximal tubule reabsorbs about 90% of glucose filtered by the kidney. Inhibiting it causes urinary loss of roughly 60–80 g of glucose per day, lowering blood glucose independently of insulin and producing a mild calorie deficit and osmotic diuresis. At the 300 mg dose canagliflozin also partly inhibits intestinal SGLT1, delaying post-meal glucose absorption.

Increased sodium delivery to the macula densa restores tubuloglomerular feedback and reduces glomerular hyperfiltration, which is thought to underlie the kidney protection seen in trials. Natriuresis, lower blood pressure, a shift toward ketone use and other haemodynamic and metabolic effects are proposed to explain heart-failure benefits that occur even without diabetes.
uses: Reduction of major cardiovascular events in type 2 diabetes with CVD
Reduction of end-stage kidney disease, creatinine doubling, cardiovascular death and HF hospitalisation in diabetic nephropathy with albuminuria

history.title: First US SGLT2 approval
history.detail: FDA approves Invokana in March 2013; EU approval follows in November 2013.

history.title: DKA warning
history.detail: FDA warns that SGLT2 inhibitors may cause ketoacidosis.

history.title: CANVAS and amputation warning
history.detail: CANVAS shows fewer cardiovascular events but about double the amputation risk; FDA adds a boxed warning.

history.title: CREDENCE
history.detail: CREDENCE stops early after showing a 30% reduction in kidney failure and related outcomes.

history.title: Boxed warning removed
history.detail: FDA removes the amputation boxed warning in August 2020, keeping a warning in the label.

serious: necrotising fasciitis of the perineum (Fournier's gangrene)

facts: Invokana was the first SGLT2 inhibitor approved by FDA (March 2013).
A boxed warning on amputation was added in 2017 and removed in 2020.
